notes.meaning: Ethan begins this song by promising to praise the Lord's faithful love forever. Even though hard times have arrived, he resolves to tell every future generation that God keeps His word. Remembering God's past mercies gives believers joy and courage when present life is dark.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Early Latin commentary treats Ethan, whose name means strong, as a picture of Christ, through whom believers receive the strength to hope in God's promises.

notes.meaning: The writer is sure that God's mercy is like a great building that rises forever and will never tumble into ruins. Earthly things constantly change, but God's faithfulness is fixed in the heavens beyond the reach of any enemy. We can trust that His goodness will outlast our deepest troubles.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Augustine explained that God's truth in keeping promises could not stand unless His mercy in forgiving sins had come first to build us up.

notes.meaning: God Himself speaks to remind His people of the covenant—a solemn binding agreement—He made with King David. He swore an oath that David's royal family and throne would endure through all generations. This royal line found its ultimate fulfillment in Jesus Christ, who reigns forever.

The angels in heaven celebrate the wondrous things God has done. In their heavenly gathering, these holy spirits constantly praise His perfect truthfulness. Even the highest spiritual beings gaze with awe at how faithfully God cares for His people.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Scholars note that while holy ones can mean believers on earth, here it specifically describes the heavenly court of angels gathered around God's throne.

notes.meaning: No created being in the skies can ever be compared to the Lord. Even the mighty angels are merely His creations and bow before Him. Because He has no equal anywhere in creation, worship belongs to Him alone.

God is deeply revered in the council of the angels who stand closest to Him. Those who serve around His throne look upon His pure majesty with holy awe. True worship always approaches the Lord with deep reverence and humility.

The Lord rules over all the heavenly armies, and no ruler can match His immense strength. His faithfulness surrounds Him like a royal robe in everything He says and does. We can rely on His power because it is always guided by His unbreakable truth.

God shows His supreme power by governing the wildest oceans. When giant waves rise up in a storm, He silences them and brings peace at His command. Just as He quiets the seas, He can bring peace to our most turbulent trials.

God shattered the proud nation of Egypt, here called Rahab, as easily as if it were a fallen corpse. By freeing Israel at the Red Sea, He scattered His foes with His mighty arm. Remembering this ancient victory gave God's people hope whenever new oppressors threatened them.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Many modern commentators suggest Rahab is an ancient image of the chaotic deep that God subdued at creation, used here poetically alongside the historical defeat of Egypt.

notes.meaning: The sky above and the world below belong to the Lord alone. He created the earth, laid its foundations, and filled it with everything that exists. Because He owns the whole universe, His people can trust Him to sustain their lives.

God designed every corner of the earth from north to south. Great peaks like Mount Tabor in the west and Mount Hermon in the east seem to shout with joy at His greatness. All creation reflects the beauty and care of its Maker.

The Lord has unmatched strength to protect the weak and overcome evil. His arm is mighty to work miracles, and His right hand is lifted up in victory. Nothing can resist His supreme power when He moves to help His servants.

Righteousness and fair justice form the firm base of God's royal throne. At the same time, His loyal love and truth go ahead of Him like royal heralds preparing His way. God's authority is comforting because He never acts cruelly or breaks a promise.

Those who recognize the joyful sound of the feast trumpets calling them to worship are truly blessed. They live and walk every day in the warm light of God's favor. Knowing God's welcoming smile gives believers steady joy and moral guidance.

God's people find ongoing reason to rejoice as they think about who He is. Because God acts righteously to save them and clear their name, they are lifted above shame and despair. Their honor does not rest on their own goodness, but on His.

The Lord Himself is the true beauty and strength of His people. In the Bible, an animal's horn is a picture of power and dignity, and God lifts up their horn by His favor. Believers give Him all the credit whenever they stand strong against trial.

The Lord is Israel's ultimate defender and shield in times of danger. The nation's king belongs to the Holy One of Israel and rules under His protection. God's people are secure because their ruler is appointed and guarded by the Lord Himself.

God spoke in a prophetic vision to His faithful messenger, promising help to defend His nation. He picked David, a brave young warrior from among the common people, to lead them. This choice reminds us that God delights to lift up the humble to do great works.

The Lord found David caring for sheep and chose him as His servant. The prophet anointed him with sacred olive oil, setting him apart to be king. This anointing also foreshadowed Jesus Christ, who was set apart and filled with the Holy Spirit without limit.

God promised to stand constantly by His chosen king to uphold him. The Lord's own arm would supply the power David needed for every battle and duty. When God gives someone a task, He always provides the strength to finish it.

No enemy would be able to conquer the king or force him to pay crushing tribute like a cruel lender over a helpless debtor. Wicked men would not succeed in grinding him down. God shielded David throughout his life from those who tried to destroy him.

The Lord pledged to crush David's enemies right before the king's eyes. Those who hated the Lord's anointed leader would face defeat and ruin. God Himself fights the battles for those who walk in His ways.

God promised that His faithful love and truth would walk beside the king every day. Through the power and authority of God's name, David's strength and honor would rise high. True victory and honor come solely from staying close to the Lord.

God promised to stretch the king's territory from the Mediterranean Sea all the way to the Euphrates River. Putting a hand over waters was a sign of taking control and ruling over the land. This vast realm pointed forward to Christ's kingdom, which spreads over every sea and shore.

The king would look up to God with childlike trust, calling Him his Father, his God, and the secure Rock of his rescue. While David experienced God's fatherly care, this was seen most clearly in Jesus Christ, who prayed to the Father through all His trials.

differ.view: Some Baptists apply these words strictly to Jesus Christ, arguing that the Old Testament saints never addressed God directly as their personal Father.
Reformed writers teach that David himself genuinely experienced God as his caring Father by covenant adoption, which then pointed forward to Christ.
